summary: "Invalid player data" error when loading a world in which you have an effect applied
description:
Workaround

Open your world’s level.dat in an NBT editor such as this one, delete Data > Player > active_effects, save the file, replace your old level.dat with the edited one and load the world again.

Attempting to load a world in which you have a potion effect fails with an “Invalid player data” error message.

This can be reproduced while riding a nautilus or giving yourself the effect using /effect and saving and leaving the world, then proceeding to play the world where you gave yourself the effect.

Expected result

The world loads as normal.

Actual result

The world fails to load, displaying a server join attempt fail message, saying “Connection Lost, Invalid player data“.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft and create a new world with default settings.
2. Enter the world and ride a nautilus until a potion effect is applied.
3. Open the Esc menu and select “Save and Quit to Title.”
4. Select “Singleplayer” and open the world again.
5. Observe that the world fails to load and displays “Connection Lost, Invalid player data.”
Observed Behavior:
### Actual behavior

After the player has an active status effect, saving and leaving the world causes the world to fail on the next load. This can occur after applying the effect with `/effect` or while riding a nautilus. Instead of entering the world, the game fails during the singleplayer server join attempt and displays:

> Connection Lost  
> Invalid player data

The world can be loaded again only after removing `Data > Player > active_effects` from the world’s `level.dat` using an NBT editor.
Expected Behavior: When loading a world after saving and leaving it while the player has an active potion effect, the world should load normally without displaying an “Invalid player data” or “Connection Lost” message. The player should be able to join and continue playing in the world, with the applied effect handled correctly rather than preventing the world from loading.
